text:
lin: Heads up, noticed a cluster of tenants with +0.4% invoice-preview deltas after router TTL tweak last night. small but customer-visible.

hazel: saw that too. initial bisect points at route-resolver returning null tag for ~0.3% of requests during briefly elevated GC window. fallback path emits a synthetic billing_event currently.

rahul: do we have example event pairs? want to check session_id and fingerprinting.

lin: pulled a couple: be_aa12, be_aa13 — same session, different event_ids; one has route_tag="fallback" and the other has route_tag=null.

hazel: query used: ```sql
SELECT session_id, event_id, route_tag, created_at, billed_tokens
FROM billing_events
WHERE session_id = 's-44f3'
ORDER BY created_at;
```

marco: quick thought: downstream aggregator assumes monotonic session sequence and dedupes by event_id only. that's brittle for retries that generate new ids.

rahul: agree. two immediate remedies: (A) make enricher emit a tombstone record when it retries so aggregator can collapse (cheap), (B) change aggregator dedupe key to (session_id, seq) and keep a short sliding window.

lin: tombstone sounds lower risk and faster. downside: needs schema bump (event_type) and consumers must interpret tombstones as cancel for prior ephemeral events.

hazel: also UX idea: mark invoice-preview rows with "provisional" when event_type=fallback or event_age < 1h. customers get context and support load drops. final invoice should never show provisional.

ops-bot: INFO: billing-preview-alert triggered at 2025-12-03T06:45Z (preview-delta: 0.42%)

marco: concern: tombstone semantics must be idempotent and order-agnostic. if tombstone arrives before canonical, we should still collapse when canonical shows up. propose tombstone carries target_event_fingerprint.

rahul: proposed tombstone payload: ```json
{
  "event_type": "tombstone",
  "target_fp": "fp:sess:44f3:seq:102",
  "emitted_by": "enricher-v2"
}
```

hazel: aggregator change minimal: check event_type, if tombstone => mark target_fp cancelled in local state for 2 minutes. also publish metric tombstone_applied_count.

lin: rollouts: short-term: UI provisional flag + add tombstone write behind feature-flag. medium-term: dedupe-by-fingerprint change in aggregator and upgrade ledger job to collapse older ephemerals.

marco: metrics and SLOs for canary: target tenants 5% then 20%. guard: invoice-preview-delta < 0.1% and tombstone_applied_rate > 95% for 2 hours.

rahul: perf estimate: tombstone adds ~0.2 extra events per 1k requests during retry storms. storage delta negligible. I'll run load replay and post numbers.

lin: nice. please add runbook steps: how to flip FF off, how to backfill tombstones if we see historical dupes, and how to escalate billing ops.

hazel: opening PRs: UI (console) https://stash.internal/redwood/console/PR/832, enricher tombstone https://stash.internal/redwood/billing/PR/671, aggregator patch https://stash.internal/redwood/ingest/PR/90

billing-bot: SCHEDULE: deploy enricher-v2 canary at 2025-12-03T13:00Z (10% tenants)

marco: also check downstream invoice-finalizer to ensure tombstones are ignored for final invoice (we don't want customers to see cancels on final billing). finalizer should only use canonical events.

lin: thanks all. post results of replay and I'll coordinate the canary with #eng-oncall.

rahul: replay done: tombstone approach in our 24h replay collapsed 91% of duplicates, added +0.4% event write volume, memory overhead <1%. attaching sim output in PR.

hazel: will update dashboard panel: billing-preview/fingerprint-dedupe and add alert when tombstone_applied_rate < 90%.

lin: perfect. moving to canary planning now. :thumbsup:
